sourceStudy.title: Study on Feng Shui (Geomantic) Suitability Evaluation of Mausoleums in Nanjing City Based on GIS
sourceStudy.studyObject: 42 protected mausoleums in Nanjing urban area; 26 additional mausoleums used for validation
sourceStudy.method: AHP-weighted information content model with sensitivity analysis

transfer: concept to measurable geographic factor architecture
separation of Long, Sha, Shui and Xue
case-study explanation in addition to map output
rebuildForTokyo: treatment of artificial terrain, culverts and buildings
rejectDirectTransfer: mausoleum suitability as a proxy for residential suitability
one final AHP score as the first product
the source text's slope bins written in kilometres; unit/method remains unresolved and is not transferable

factorTranslation.notes: Separate natural-terrain roughness from building-height roughness.
Absolute elevation is weak in Tokyo; use relative position within each landform context.
Interpret enclosure directionally rather than as undirected hill density.

tokyoReplacement: continuous ridgeline rather than nearest peak
factorTranslation.notes: Tokyo has subdued uplands; local ridge shoulders can matter more than mountain peaks.
Keep natural and artificial drainage outlets separate.
Distance alone is insufficient. Surface-water relation and underground continuity are different objects.
Use degrees/percent slope and geomorphic stability; never use the source paper's kilometre-labelled bins.
Terrain aspect and dwelling orientation are separate.

tokyoAdditionalFactors.name: ridge_network_continuity
tokyoAdditionalFactors.reason: Long is a connected morphology; nearest height alone cannot represent it.

tokyoAdditionalFactors.name: historical_water_continuity
tokyoAdditionalFactors.reason: Tokyo's rivers and valleys are frequently culverted, filled or urbanized.

tokyoAdditionalFactors.name: observed_groundwater_and_geology
tokyoAdditionalFactors.reason: UNDERLAND can separate historical-water symbolism from current dampness and subsurface conditions.

tokyoAdditionalFactors.name: artificial_severance_and_cut_fill
tokyoAdditionalFactors.reason: Railways, arterial roads, excavation and embankment reshape subdued urban landforms.

tokyoAdditionalFactors.name: shrine_temple_ritual_relation
tokyoAdditionalFactors.reason: Ritual sites may preserve settlement, boundary, water-management and disaster-memory relations; distance alone is not meaning.

tokyoAdditionalFactors.name: dampness_ventilation_solar
tokyoAdditionalFactors.reason: The target use is housing, so symbolic suitability and practical habitability must be displayed separately.

modelingPlan.phase0: compute transparent factor layers without final weights
modelingPlan.phase1: historical-site and shrine relation analysis with matched and random controls
modelingPlan.phase2: spatial block validation by municipality and landform
modelingPlan.phase3: derive interpretable weights or non-linear relationships only after holdout evidence
modelingPlan.phase4: personal-sense blind comparison after proxy freeze
candidateMethods: AHP as a documented expert scenario, not the sole truth
